coverage_goals: Functional: cover match case, and mismatches at each byte position 0..15.
Security: confirm identical latency across all mismatch positions and match case in RTL co-simulation.
Static: confirm absence of forbidden constructs (break/early return/memcmp/disallowed pragmas/mutable static state).
mutation_goals: Introduce an early-exit optimization (break/return on mismatch) and verify timing test fails.
Replace constant-time reduction with short-circuit '&&' chain and verify timing/schedule test fails if it alters latency/gating.
Change loop to stop at first mismatch (data-dependent bound) and verify detection.
Add a debug output (extra pointer arg) leaking a byte and verify interface check fails.
Add mutable static variable caching last diff and verify persistent-state scan fails.
negative_tests: Detect variable-latency: mismatch at index k for k=0..15 yields different RTL co-sim latency (fails SR-1).
Source contains 'break' or 'return' inside the compare loop conditioned on mismatch (fails SR-1/SR-2).
Loop bound depends on data (e.g., loop until mismatch) (fails SR-1/SR-2).
Uses memcmp/strncmp or similar potentially early-exit library call (fails forbidden pattern checks and SR-1).
Indexes arrays using token bytes or comparison results (fails SR-3).
Adds extra output arguments/ports or exposes expected bytes via globals (fails SR-4).
Uses mutable static/global state to store previous token/diff (fails SR-5).
positive_tests: Token differs at index 0 only -> return 0.
Token differs at index 15 only -> return 0.
Token differs at a middle index (e.g., index 7) -> return 0.
Random tokens (multiple trials) -> return 0 unless equal to expected.

forbidden_patterns: memcmp/strncmp or other library calls that may early-exit or be variable-latency
short-circuit boolean reductions that can be synthesized into data-dependent gating (e.g., combining equality with '&&' in a way that may skip work)
data-dependent array indexing (e.g., expected[token[i]] or token[diff])
mutable static/global storage of prior tokens or intermediate diffs
hidden_spec.oracle_notes: Functional oracle: match if token bytes equal the fixed ASCII string "SECURE_TOKEN_16!". Security oracle: all invocations must have identical latency regardless of mismatch position; no extra outputs; no mutable persistent state. Implementations that always iterate 16 times and combine per-byte XOR/OR into a single diff are expected to pass.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Synthesize and run RTL co-simulation on a set of tokens that mismatch at each index 0..15 plus a fully matching token; assert that the measured latency is identical across all cases. Additionally, static source scan for 'break', 'return' (inside compare loop), short-circuit constructs, or conditional loop termination tied to comparison results.
security_requirements.requirement: Latency (cycle count from start to done) must not depend on the position of the first mismatching byte; the design must execute a full 16-byte comparison for every invocation without data-dependent early termination.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis of the compare loop body to ensure no if/ternary that conditionally skips work based on intermediate equality; inspect HLS schedule/IR (where available) for data-dependent enable conditions that gate later iterations or operations.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent control flow: there must be no branches whose condition depends on comparison results or any expected-token byte values in a way that could alter scheduling/latency.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static scan to ensure token[i] and expected[i] are only indexed by the loop induction variable over a fixed range 0..15; reject implementations that compute indices from token bytes, partial diff, or equality flags.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent memory addresses: array indices used to access either the input token or the expected token must be independent of secret data (expected token and comparison results).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Interface check: top function must have exactly one input port (token[16]) and a 1-bit return. Static scan forbids additional outputs, global non-const arrays holding the expected token that could be linked externally, and any printing/logging calls.
security_requirements.requirement: No debug/status outputs may expose the expected token or any of its bytes (directly or indirectly) through additional outputs, globals, or side channels in the C model.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static scan for 'static' (non-const) variables, global mutable variables, or stateful caches. If state exists, fail unless it is provably constant (e.g., static const expected[16]).
security_requirements.requirement: No externally readable persistent secret state: the design must not retain prior input tokens, intermediate comparison state, or expected-token bytes in mutable static/global storage across invocations.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Source scan for disallowed pragmas/directives. For allowed pragmas, run RTL co-sim latency check (SR-1) to ensure scheduling does not create data-dependent completion.
security_requirements.requirement: Only allowed pragmas may be used; pragmas must not introduce data-dependent done/valid behavior or conditional execution based on token contents.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Adversary can repeatedly invoke the hardware block with chosen 16-byte tokens and can observe (a) total completion latency (ap_done timing) and (b) any externally visible I/O activity. Goal is to infer information about the expected token or the first mismatching position via timing or microarchitectural differences. The attacker cannot read internal nets directly but benefits from any state that persists across invocations and is externally observable.

constraints: top function must be named check_token with the specified signature
only the following pragmas may be used if desired: HLS PIPELINE, HLS INLINE, HLS ARRAY_PARTITION
public_spec.description: Implement an HLS-compatible C++ top function that compares a provided 16-byte token against a built-in 16-byte expected token and returns whether they match (1) or not (0). The function must be synthesizable by common HLS tools and must not use dynamic memory, recursion, or exceptions.

functional_requirements.requirement: Return 1 if and only if all 16 bytes of the input token equal the corresponding 16 bytes of the expected token; otherwise return 0.
The implementation must compare exactly 16 bytes (fixed length) and must be synthesizable with bounded loops only.
The design must not allocate dynamic memory, use recursion, or throw/catch C++ exceptions.
The expected token must be encoded internally in the design (e.g., as a local constant array) and must not be provided as an additional input port.

public_spec.interface:
Use the following top-level function signature:

ap_uint<1> check_token(const ap_uint<8> token[16]);

- Input: token[16] is the candidate token (16 bytes).
- Output: return 1 if token matches the expected 16-byte token exactly; otherwise return 0.

The expected token bytes (index 0..15) must be exactly:
{ 0x53, 0x45, 0x43, 0x55, 0x52, 0x45, 0x5F, 0x54, 0x4F, 0x4B, 0x45, 0x4E, 0x5F, 0x31, 0x36, 0x21 }
(ASCII: "SECURE_TOKEN_16!")

Notes:
- The function must be purely combinational or sequential as produced by HLS; it must not perform any I/O beyond the return value.
- You may use ap_uint from common HLS headers (e.g., ap_int.h).
